resources.string: Your data stays on your phone.

Every app you watch lives here as a little creature. It grows a bit each time its app contacts a website or service. Snoops (companies that collect data about you) sit next to the apps they visit. Tap a creature or a Snoop to learn more. The sky follows your phone\'s clock.
Pick the apps Mycelium should watch. Only these apps go through Mycelium; all other apps are left completely alone. You can change this any time.
What your watched apps did, newest first, grouped by app. Each card is one contact: the app reaching out to a website or service. Mycelium sees which one, never what was sent.
A few big facts about your watched apps for today or this week, and one chart of when they were busy.
Ask in plain words. The Gardener answers only from what this phone has seen, works offline, and never guesses. Each answer can show the exact moments it is based on (tap Details).
A checklist of phone settings that help Mycelium see clearly and keep running. Tap Fix to jump to the right setting.
Change the look and motion, manage protection and Snoops you shooed away, add your own AI key, and look after your data.
Short answers to common questions, and what Mycelium\'s words mean.
What stays on your phone, what can leave it, why Mycelium needs each permission, and who made the parts of this app.
Tools for curious people and developers: ask the database directly, export or wipe it, run a demo, and see technical details. Off by default.
An honest list of what Mycelium does not see or stop, so you know what to expect.
Mycelium is built with free and open-source parts. Here are their names and license texts.
Mycelium is watching %1$s. Everything it notices stays on this phone.

No internet right now. Mycelium answers your apps on the phone and sends nothing. It sorts what it caught when you\'re back online.

Pick at least one app to watch first.

Protected: Mycelium is watching your chosen apps. Paused: it is off and keeps nothing. Safe Mode (offline): there is no internet, so it answers apps on the phone and sorts what it caught later.\n\nProtection uses Android\'s VPN feature, but only locally: Mycelium is not a VPN service, and nothing is sent to a server.

To notice which websites and services your chosen apps contact, Mycelium uses Android\'s VPN feature. It runs only on this phone: your traffic is not sent to any server of ours, and other apps are not touched. Android shows a key icon while it\'s on.

Each bar is an hour (today) or a day (this week). Green is all contacts; red is the part that went to Snoops.
Hi! I\'m the Gardener. Ask me about your watched apps, like \"What just happened?\". I only know what this phone has seen, and I never guess.

Optional. With your own key and internet, a cloud AI can phrase the answer. Before anything is sent you see exactly what would go out, and nothing leaves until you tap Send. Without it, the Gardener answers right here on your phone.
Want an AI to phrase answers? Add your own key in Settings › Optional AI.

resources.string: Mycelium is helpful, but not magic. Here\'s exactly what it can and can\'t do.
For the apps you choose: the name of each website or service they contact, when, and whether you were using the app. It can shoo Snoops away from those apps.
What it can\'t see or stop

string-array.name: limits_t
string-array.item: Messages, photos and contents
Apps that hide their contacts
Apps you didn\'t choose
All tracking
Exact data use, right now
Who you are

string-array.name: limits_b
string-array.item: It sees only the name of a website, never what is sent or received.
Some apps use their own private connection (for example \"secure DNS\") or fixed addresses. Mycelium can\'t see or shoo those away. Private DNS in your phone settings hides everything from it.
Only apps you switched on in My Apps go through Mycelium.
Snoops can also collect data through the app\'s own servers, or by other means. Shooing away helps, but it never stops all tracking.
Android counts data in blocks of about two hours, so the newest use shows up a little later.
Mycelium has no account and never knows your name. It doesn\'t need to.

resources.string: Your data is kept and processed on your device.
Every contact, Snoop visit, number, alert and Gardener answer is noticed, worked out and kept on this phone. There is no account, no analytics and no server of ours.
Only when you add your own AI key, switch on the AI helper and tap Send: the facts shown in the preview go to that AI provider. Nothing else, ever.
What Android lets Mycelium do, in plain words. You can review or remove any of them in Android\'s app settings.
